positions.commentary: Nvidia's market value grew from $626 million to $5 trillion, representing an appreciation of around 8,000X over 26 plus years.
Microsoft's PE ratio is currently half of what it was 26 years ago.
Alphabet is among the biggest AI players with lower PE ratios today compared to the 1998-2000 bubble.
Amazon is among the biggest AI players with lower PE ratios today compared to the 1998-2000 bubble.
Meta is among the biggest AI players with lower PE ratios today compared to the 1998-2000 bubble.
Oracle had much higher PE ratios during the 1998-2000 internet bubble than today's AI players.
Cisco had much higher PE ratios during the 1998-2000 internet bubble than today's AI players.

thesis: This episode argues that while major tech firms like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google are making sound, reasonable investments in AI infrastructure using their cash reserves, the market has overreacted to Google's progress, erasing $115 billion in NVIDIA's value. It suggests that current valuations for AI leaders are actually lower than during the 1998-2000 bubble, yet specific criticisms persist regarding NVIDIA's circular deals and the sharp decline in its stock price.

claims.claim: Nvidia is criticized for making circular deals where it invests in OpenAI to buy its own chips, and Goldman Sachs estimates 15% of its sales will come from these deals.
claims.quote: Nvidia has also made some deals that have raised questions about whether the company is paying itself. It announced that it would invest $100 billion in Open AI. The startup receives that money as it buys or leases Nvidia's chips. Goldman Sachs has estimated that Nvidia will make 15% of its sales next year from what critics also call circular deals.

claims.claim: Nvidia's market value grew from $626 million to $5 trillion, representing an appreciation of around 8,000X over 26 plus years.

claims.claim: OpenAI is criticized for making circular deals with chip makers, cloud computing companies, and others, and for having made investment commitments totaling $1.4 trillion despite not turning a profit.
claims.quote: Adding to worries critics say some of the deals that open AI has made with chip makers, cloud computing companies, and others are oddly circular.
